declared_by: drafted by a coding agent (Claude Code) before any screen result was computed; not revised after seeing results
why_a_separate_manifest: methods/three_arm_statistics.md requires that a larger trait screen declare its own candidate manifest rather than reuse the frozen six-trait family. The six Table 1 traits keep their own family and their own published q-values; this screen neither replaces nor recorrects them.
candidate_rule: every retained trait column of the pinned profile matrix, in header order: all columns except the three identifier columns and every MediaDive growth-medium column. The candidate set is read from the matrix at run time and never hard-coded, so a corpus change moves the family rather than silently mismatching it.
base_population: human experiments with exactly one increased and one decreased profile (load_profiles, paired, human)
denominator: sum of all retained non-MediaDive trait columns of the profile, including traits outside Table 1; selecting a candidate never redefines this total
study_weighting: mean fraction per direction within study, then one vote per study; each eligible study weighted equally
test: two-sided exact binomial test of non-tied studies shifting up against 0.5, with an exact 95% Clopper-Pearson interval for that share. Identical to the six-trait arm; only the family it is corrected in changes.

correction.primary: Benjamini-Yekutieli across the full candidate family
correction.why: the candidates are strongly and positively dependent (#265), and PR #181 already applies BY to the 15-ratio family for the same reason. BY is valid under arbitrary dependence; BH is reported beside it for comparability with the other two arms, which use BH.
correction.also_reported: Benjamini-Hochberg across the same full family
correction.not_done: no correction is ever recomputed over a cross-arm overlap or over a displayed subset

effective_family_size.why_excluded: known to be anticonservative under strong positive dependence; named here rather than silently omitted (#265 item 2). It is computed and written to the family table carrying this exclusion, so a reader can see the disagreement.
effective_family_size.use: the significant set is reported at the nominal family size and again at the effective family size, as a sensitivity pair. Membership stability between the two is reported; neither is presented as the corrected result on its own.

correlation_bases.primary: Spearman between traits over the study-level contrasts actually tested
correlation_bases.secondary: Spearman between traits over profiles, the basis quoted in #263 and #265, retained so those figures can be reproduced and checked

threshold_note: both thresholds are reported for every candidate; no candidate is dropped from the table by either. The screen selects nothing.

states_kept_explicit.tested: at least one non-tied study contrast
states_kept_explicit.all_tied: every eligible study contrast is within the tie tolerance; no p and no q, never a share of 0 or a p of 1
states_kept_explicit.no_eligible_studies: no study contributes a contrast for this trait; no p and no q

highlighted_subset: the six Table 1 traits are flagged in the output as a subset of the full family, not as the family. Their separately published six-trait BH q-values are unchanged by this screen; changing any manuscript number is #205.

amendments.change: effective_family_size.use is superseded for reporting: the reported significant set is Benjamini-Yekutieli at the nominal family size, with Benjamini-Hochberg at the nominal size beside it. The effective-size set is a sensitivity bound with no FDR guarantee, and the count is reported as unstable rather than as either number alone.
amendments.reason: ruling on #265 by the PI (2026-09-28): Li & Ji and Galwey set per-test familywise thresholds, so substituting their m into BH or BY is a heuristic, and BY at the nominal m already controls FDR under arbitrary dependence.
amendments.known_when_amended: the full screen result: 18 traits at BY q <= 0.05 with m = 317, 56 with m = 112.
amendments.unchanged: the candidate rule, the test, both corrections, both family sizes and every output column; only which column the reporting leads with

amendments.change: effective_family_size.why_excluded is corrected. Cheverud/Nyholt is excluded as an unreliable estimator that disagrees with Li & Ji and Galwey (Li & Ji 2005), not as anticonservative.
amendments.reason: #325: on this corpus Cheverud/Nyholt gives the largest effective m of the three (294.4 vs Li & Ji 112.0 on the contrast basis; 198.9 vs 60.0 on the profile basis), so it would give the strictest correction, the opposite of the original rationale.
amendments.known_when_amended: the full screen result, including the family table above.
amendments.unchanged: which estimators are reported and which is excluded; every number and output column
